plain: A person who kills a public figure by surprise, often for political reasons.

webster.text: One who kills or attempts to kill, by surprise or secret assault.

example.quote: We are told by Sully that this was the favorite pursuit of that good king during the last years of his life; and he would probably have carried it into execution, had not the dagger of an assassin deprived the world of his valuable life.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Pennsylvania Convention, Mr. WILSON, December 11, 1787 and the following sittings (Elliot prints no later date headings) (2d ed. 1836)
